blocks.text: Initial management of Acute Ischemic Stroke

Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a leading cause of adult disability in the developed world. In AIS, thrombus impairs cerebral blood flow, resulting in brain tissue infarction. Collateral blood flow gives rise to an area of hypo perfused tissue (ischemic penumbra) that is at risk of infarction if hypoperfusion persists. Prompt reopening of an occluded blood vessel to re-establish blood flow to the ischemic area (reperfusion) in eligible patients, can rescue the ischemic penumbra from death and spare the patient from serious long-term disabilities.

Epilepsy is a common neurological disorder characterised by recurring seizures. About two-thirds of people with active epilepsy have their epilepsy controlled satisfactorily with anti-seizure medication (ASM). Other treatment approaches may include surgery and neuromodulation. Optimal management is required to improve patient’s health outcomes and minimise detrimental impacts on social, educational, and occupational activities.
